title: This Paradoxical Desert Landscape Is Filled with Fresh Water
gist: A NASA Landsat 9 satellite view of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park in northeastern Brazil shows a sand-dune field studded with freshwater lagoons and ringed by ocean and forest — a desert-form landscape that is not water-poor. Short photo-led item with no data beyond the imagery description.

insights.claim: Lençóis Maranhenses National Park in northeastern Brazil combines vast sandy dunes with an unusually high density of freshwater lagoons, functioning as a desert-form landscape with water everywhere.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Dune morphology alone is a poor proxy for aridity or water availability in remote-sensing land classification.
insights.quote: Basically, it’s a desert with an oasis everywhere you turn.
insights.locator: What makes the region such a paradox

insights.claim: The dune field is bounded by ocean on one side and forest on the other, making it an ecological transition zone rather than an isolated desert interior.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Context for why the water table sits high enough to fill inter-dune depressions.
insights.locator: COMPLEX ECOSYSTEM: The dunes in Lençóis

themes.theme: Satellite imaging as the only adequate viewpoint

insights.claim: NASA Landsat 9 imagery is what makes the lagoon pattern legible — the lagoons register only as subtle blue specks inside the tan dune field, and the structure is not apparent from the ground.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Example of orbital imagery revealing landscape structure invisible at ground scale; relevant to earth-observation data use cases.
insights.locator: you really need to see them from above
